chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about a man who hunts a bird that is worth many dirhams, and it is level-winged (capable of flight), and its owner is known, or it comes to him and he seeks it, from one who does not accuse him (of stealing it). He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not permissible for him to keep it; he should return it to him.' So I said to him (peace be upon him): 'And if he hunts what has no control over its two wings, and its seeker is not known? He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is for him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on keeping a hunted bird if its owner is unknown?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the distinction between a lost domesticated bird (which retains its owner's rights) and a wild bird, establishing that ownership is determined by the ability to identify the owner through a trustworthy witness. This ruling underscores the Shia legal principle of preserving property rights (Hifz al-Mal) while allowing acquisition of unowned resources, reflecting the practical application of *ghanimat* (spoils/finder's keepers) in daily life. The hadith highlights the importance of social trust mechanisms in pre-modern Islamic societies for resolving property disputes without litigation.

en.hubeali: A number of our companons, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> about a man who hunts the birds which are worth a lot of Dirhams, and its two wings are level, and its owner is known, or he comes over, so he seeks it, one who does not accuse him (of stealing it). He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not Permissible for him to keep it. He should return it to him’. So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So if he hunts what has no control over its two wings, its seeker not known?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is for him’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr who has said the following: “I once asked al-Rida 5 , ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who hunts a bird which is worth a large amount of dirham and it has leveled wings. He knows the owner of the bird or that he comes to ask about the bird but does not accuse him. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not lawful for him to keep. He must return it to him.’
I then asked, ‘What happens if he hunts that which has control over its wings and no one asking for it is known ? 5 He (the Imam) said, ‘It becomes his property. 5 ”
